target: Synthetic localhost fixture with deliberate faults
environment: Python Playwright using installed Microsoft Edge 157.0.4341.60
scope: Synthetic async wait, unit and capacity examples. Intentional fixture faults illustrate reporting. Capacity measures local CSV reads only.
cleanup: The demo service stopped and discarded its in-memory jobs. Temporary CSV files were removed.
next_steps: The largest local CSV checked was 10,000 rows. No application capacity limit was established.
Use the target README, documented completion signals and independent data on the QA application.

requirements.claim: The UI publishes the correct result for the accepted job.
Generate deterministic rows and exact amount metadata.

cases.expected: The heading and report button are ready.
steps: Open the synthetic home URL.
Verify heading and enabled report button.

cases.expected: The new report publishes exactly 3 rows for its own job ID.
cases.oracle: Synthetic fixture expects a 3-row result for the accepted ID.
steps: Select success on the synthetic report page.
Submit once and capture the 202 response and job ID.
Read the documented status and verify the result for the same job.
cases.observed: The correlated job finished. The new UI result displayed 3 rows after publication.

cases.expected: The documented terminal failure appears and preserves the previous published result.
cases.oracle: Synthetic negative fixture explicitly terminates as failed.
steps: Select failure on the synthetic report page.
Submit once and capture the 202 response and job ID.
Read the documented status and verify the result for the same job.
cases.observed: Terminal failure reached. UI displayed Failed and preserved the previous result.

cases.expected: The new report publishes exactly 3 rows for its own job ID.

steps: Select timeout on the synthetic report page.
Submit once and capture the 202 response and job ID.
Read the documented status and verify the result for the same job.
cases.observed: The synthetic job stayed running beyond the configured deadline.
cases.cause_detail: The fixture deliberately keeps the state running.
cases.recommendation: Check whether the worker advances the job or emits a terminal failure when processing ends.
cases.verification: Rerun the job and confirm a terminal status within the agreed deadline, followed by correct output.

cases.expected: The new report publishes exactly 3 rows for its own job ID.
cases.oracle: Synthetic fixture expects a 3-row result for the accepted ID.
steps: Select wrong-job on the synthetic report page.
Submit once and capture the 202 response and job ID.
Read the documented status and verify the result for the same job.
cases.observed: The injected status response carried a different job ID and was rejected.
cases.cause_detail: The fixture intentionally substitutes another job ID in the response.
cases.recommendation: Key status lookups and serialization by the submitted job ID.
cases.verification: Submit two independent jobs and assert each status payload matches its requested ID.

cases.expected: The new report publishes exactly 3 rows for its own job ID.
cases.oracle: Synthetic fixture expects a 3-row result for the accepted ID.
steps: Select bad-output on the synthetic report page.
Submit once and capture the 202 response and job ID.
Read the documented status and verify the result for the same job.
cases.observed: The completed job and its new UI result contained 2 rows instead of the expected 3.
cases.cause_detail: The fixture injects an incorrect row count before publishing it.
cases.recommendation: Trace the discrepancy in the generated result before publication. Compare the payload with the independently expected row count.
cases.verification: Rerun with the same input and assert exact output in both the status result and browser.

cases.expected: Check the published status for the approver's own test record.
cases.observed: The synthetic report fixture has no approver account or approval workflow.
cases.next_step: Run on an authorized QA application with the approver role.
